subtype: Approach: assuming it will never happen [Pitfall]
passage: "Boring," said Yogesh when Papa unrolled the fire-drill card on the sofa. "Fires only happen to strangers." He rolled his eyes and went back to his game. Three weeks later, in the kitchen, the burner flame jumped to the curtain. Yogesh stood with a glass in his hand, staring. Which door? Which way? What was step one? The steps he had laughed at were nowhere in his head. "Out! Now!" His father Jagdish grabbed his arm, pulled him into the corridor and shut the door, while Mummy shouted for the neighbours and rang the fire brigade. Downstairs, Yogesh's knees shook. He had stood still for far too long.

qa.q: Who pulled Yogesh out of the kitchen?
qa.a: His father Jagdish pulled him out.

qa.q: What was Yogesh feeling as he stood in the kitchen with the glass?
qa.a: Frozen and scared, and confused, since none of the steps he had laughed at came to mind.

qa.q: What would you advise Yogesh to do now, and why?
qa.a: Yogesh could ask to practise the drill again and take it seriously, because knowing the steps lets his body move when he is frightened.

qa.q: What might Jagdish be feeling as he pulls Yogesh into the corridor?
qa.a: Jagdish is likely frightened and urgent, wanting only to get his son out, and probably relieved once they are outside.

grounding: A boy dismisses fire drills as boring, so when the kitchen catches fire he hesitates and cannot remember the steps.

subtype: Approach: assuming it will never happen [Pitfall]
passage:
"Tushar, come for the drill."
"Papa, this is so boring. Fires don't happen to us."
"Just walk the route once."
"Next time."
Two weeks later.
"Mohit! Something's burning!"
"Tushar, the pan's caught fire! Out, now!"
"Where... which way?"
"The door! Go!"
Tushar stood frozen in the kitchen doorway.
Mohit grabbed his hand and pulled him out to the stairs. Their father turned off the gas at the cylinder, covered the pan with a damp cloth and followed them down. The fire went out. Nobody was hurt.
Outside, Tushar was shaking. "I didn't know what to do."
"That's why we practise," Mohit said quietly.

qa.q: What did their father cover the pan with?
How was Tushar feeling as he stood in the kitchen doorway?
qa.a: He was frozen with fear and confusion, unsure what to do because he had never practised.

qa.q: What would you change first for Tushar, and why?
qa.a: Walk the escape route with the family the next day, because practising makes the steps automatic when fear hits.

qa.q: How does the fire look to Mohit?
qa.a: Mohit is scared but acts fast, pulling his brother out, and quietly points out why the drill matters.

grounding: It shows a boy laughing off the family drill as boring, and then hesitating and not remembering the steps when the kitchen gas catches.

subtype: Approach: assuming it will never happen [Pitfall]
passage: Last winter I thought fire drills were for other families. When Papa wanted us to practise, I rolled my eyes and went back to my game. Then one evening the gas stove flared while Amma was frying, and flames jumped up from the pan. Amma shouted, "Darshan, out! Take Kavitha!" And I just stood there. My legs wouldn't go. I didn't remember which way to run. My little sister Kavitha tugged my hand and we went to the door. Amma turned off the cylinder and covered the pan, and our neighbour came running with a fire blanket. Nobody was hurt. But I haven't rolled my eyes at a drill since.

qa.q: Who came running with a fire blanket?
qa.a: Their neighbour came with a fire blanket.

qa.q: How did Darshan feel standing in the kitchen?
qa.a: Darshan felt frozen and scared, unable to remember which way to go.

qa.q: What else could Darshan's family do to make sure everyone is ready?
qa.a: They could practise the drill once a month, so the steps are fresh for everyone.

qa.q: How does the evening look to Kavitha?
qa.a: Kavitha, though little, is the one who tugs her sibling's hand, so she may have felt scared but brave.

grounding: It shows a child who laughed off fire drills freezing when the kitchen gas catches, because the steps were never practised.
